indicators.note: the word in tells us the zero is placed within the other word

parts.note: through, as in passing through the trees, means between them
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Advice to say nothing at all in the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like a verb (speak), but it is the adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: An utter fool is a complete, out-and-out one, a synonym sense.

explanation.surface: A new kind of headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilby is George du Maurier's 1894 novel, and the soft felt hat with a dented crown took its name from a stage version of it.

indicators.note: the moon's name can be seen inside the run of letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A moon that can only be seen in one autumn month.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is one of the moons of Uranus, named after Shakespeare's fairy king.

clue.text: Work with one in fashion, as an alternative

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: in tells us the one goes inside the word for fashion

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style, as in bon ton
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A job with a fashion house as another career path.
explanation.walkthrough: TON for fashion, as in 'bon ton', is a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is a choice you may take instead of another, a synonym.

clue.text: The sort of adhesive used by the foreman?

definitions.text: The sort of adhesive used by the foreman?

parts.words: The sort of adhesive used by the foreman?
parts.note: a foreman is informally called a gaffer, so his sticky tape would bear his name; the real product is strong cloth tape used by film and stage crews

explanation.surface: A question about which glue the site boss favours.
explanation.definitionFit: This cloth-backed sticky strip is named after the gaffer, the chief lighting electrician on a film set.

clue.text: Difficult at university, short of money

parts.note: difficult means hard
to be up is to be in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A student finding life tough and broke.
explanation.definitionFit: To be broke or lacking cash is a common idiom with this phrase.

clue.text: Fabulous runner's article printed in US state capital

indicators.note: printed in suggests the letter is set into the text of the city's name

parts.note: Atlanta is the capital of Georgia
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news item about a runner appears in a Georgia newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from a fable or myth, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Atalanta is the swift huntress of Greek myth who lost a race by stopping for golden apples.

clue.text: Dog breed — Cornishman nervously holds Peke's lead

indicators.note: acting nervously suggests jittery movement, so the letters are jumbled
the lead of the Peke is its front, its first letter

explanation.surface: A man from Cornwall anxiously holds a Pekingese's leash at a dog show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog breed' reads as the definition, but 'breed' is fodder: BREED, CORNISHMAN and P are all shuffled, with 'holds' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This German guard-dog breed, sleek and tan-and-black, is a dog by example.

explanation.surface: Pick out a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify is to pick out or recognise, and also to associate, as in identifying with a cause.

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
b is an abbreviation for barrels in oil-industry figures
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rickety lorry loaded with casks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flimsy' is a noun here: thin copy paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A flimsy is a thin sheet used for duplicates, the old typing copy made with such paper.

clue.text: Tarnish one's good reputation as a penman?

definitions.text: Tarnish one's good reputation as a penman?

parts.words: Tarnish one's good reputation as a penman?
parts.note: the idiom for spoiling a clean record, read literally as dropping ink on a handwriting practice book

explanation.surface: A writer's standing is spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means spoil a good record, from an ink spill on a model handwriting exercise book.

clue.text: Material's excellent, providing good opportunities for laughter, mostly

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means excellent

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: rich means highly amusing, as in 'that's rich'

explanation.surface: Praise for a funny script.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth, a synonym for material in the textile sense.

parts.note: inexpensive means cheap
the skate is a flat ray-like fish

explanation.surface: A tightwad who wants a bargain fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person, a synonym for a miser.

clue.text: Dramatist to stay with friend in America

parts.note: to stop at a hotel is to stay there
pard is American slang for partner or friend

explanation.surface: A playwright stays with a buddy in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Stoppard was a British playwright, author of Arcadia, so an example of a dramatist.

indicators.note: around means the job word is placed round the hospital letter

parts.note: a task is a job
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Working in the capital in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan, an example of a capital city.

clue.text: I'm perfectly capable of acting like you in Chess?

definitions.text: I'm perfectly capable of acting like you in Chess?

parts.words: I'm perfectly capable of acting like you in Chess?
parts.note: a warning that I can retaliate in kind, read as a remark about two players in the game of chess

explanation.surface: A chess player bragging that they can mimic their opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying warns that someone else can retaliate using the same unfair tactics.

indicators.note: aboard means the husband letter goes on board, inside the other word

parts.note: dingy means drab and discoloured

explanation.surface: A spouse on a shabby little craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small boat, an example.

parts.note: Alice is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A wife showing ill will.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is ill will, a synonym for spite.

indicators.note: two thirds of the three-letter word means its first two letters

parts.note: veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: Removing the lid to show some rare meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to expose or disclose, a synonym for uncover.

clue.text: First to purchase C. Hoy's remarkable film

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken
remarkable suggests something altered strikingly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Chris Hoy is a British Olympic track cyclist

explanation.surface: Buying the cyclist's extraordinary movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Chris Hoy is a Scottish Olympic cycling champion; the 's is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is Hitchcock's 1960 thriller, an example of a film.

clue.text: The French don't like illegal broadcaster

parts.note: as means like
a pirate radio station broadcasts without a licence

explanation.surface: A complaint that the French dislike unlicensed radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't like' looks like one phrase, but 'like' is AS: the definition stops at 'don't', since French speakers leave the H unsounded.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspirate is to sound an H with a breath, which French speakers do not do.

clue.text: Bird's eggs returned by Church of England priest, ultimately

indicators.note: returned means the word for eggs is read backwards

parts.note: ova are eggs

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A vicar hands back a bird's eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upcurved bill, an example.

indicators.note: on means the fire word comes after the other in this across entry

parts.note: to deck a room is to hang it with decorations
a conflagration is a fire

explanation.surface: A blaze on a ship's deck causes hold-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' suggests a ship but is a verb: to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang fire is to hesitate or hold off, an idiom for postponing.

clue.text: Facts about fine revolutionary World War II aircraft

indicators.note: about means the facts word is placed around the other piece

parts.note: data are facts

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: OK means fine

explanation.surface: Information on a well-preserved wartime plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas Dakota was the RAF name for the C-47 transport plane, an example.

parts.note: so, as in so good, means very
well, as in 'it would be well to wait', means advisable

explanation.surface: Agreeing that something is wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying this phrase signals agreement or acceptance, an exclamation of assent.
